title: Luanda Summit Mobilises Over $44 Billion for Africa's Infrastructure Drive
body: The four-day Luanda Summit on Financing Infrastructure Development in Africa closed with commitments exceeding $44 billion from governments, development agencies and private investors. The pledges target energy, transport, water, telecommunications and technology projects, and are expected to complement AfCFTA-driven regional integration. Organisers framed the outcome against Africa's estimated $100 billion annual infrastructure financing gap cited by the African Development Bank.

title: Third Russia-Africa Summit Opens in Moscow with Trade, Energy and Nuclear Cooperation on the Agenda
body: The summit opened October 28 at Moscow's Gostiny Dvor under the theme "For Peace, Security and Development", drawing leaders from across the continent. Priority topics include trade and investment, peaceful nuclear energy, independent payment systems, food security and digital adoption. Namibia's President Nandi-Ndaitwah arrived seeking trade, investment and mineral-beneficiation deals, with Rosatom still promoting its suspended Headspring uranium project in Omaheke.

title: Africa CDC Convenes Ministers as Ebola Outbreak Spreads Across Three Regions
body: Africa CDC convened a high-level virtual meeting of African Ministers of Health on October 28 as the Ebola outbreak escalated across three regions of the continent. The agency flagged late detection in Nigeria as an alarm bell as the disease continued to spread.

title: Liberia Opens First Dedicated Mining and Energy Investment Conference (LIMEC 2026)
body: Liberia's first dedicated mining and energy investment conference, LIMEC 2026, opened in Monrovia on October 28 with President Joseph Boakai delivering the keynote, running through October 29. Organised by the Ministry of Mines and Energy with AME Trade, and platinum-sponsored by ArcelorMittal Liberia and Avesoro Resources, it pitches the country's resource wealth as a driver of jobs and economic growth.

title: Dangote Refinery IPO Closes as Africa's First Pan-African Public Offering
body: Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals has closed its Initial Public Offering (IPO) on October 27, 2026, attracting subscriptions from investors in over 90 countries, including 51 of Africa's 54 nations. Described as Africa's first truly pan-African public offering, the N2.15 trillion raise marks a significant milestone in continental capital-market development and industrial ownership.

title: Afreximbank and South Africa IDC sign $8bn industrial finance partnership
body: Afreximbank and South Africa's Industrial Development Corporation signed a Memorandum of Understanding in Cairo to jointly originate, finance and monitor projects strengthening South Africa's industrial base and regional value chains. The three-year partnership combines Afreximbank's trade finance reach with IDC's project development and underwriting capacity, and is aimed at accelerating trade under AfCFTA.

title: NSIA Prize for Innovation awards seven Nigerian startups over $275,000
body: At the fourth NSIA Prize for Innovation Demo Day in Abuja, seven startups shared cash and equity prizes of roughly $275,000-$277,000, drawn from more than 6,000 applications. Come Again Foods won first place with a package of about $100,000, followed by Protein Kapital ($70,000) and AI teleradiology firm InstantRad ($50,000). The prize focused on manufacturing, climate and food security, and healthcare.

title: South Africa proposes Synthetic Financial Centre to relax 45% offshore cap
body: The South African Reserve Bank published a draft framework for a Synthetic Financial Centre that would let approved asset managers, banks and insurers manage foreign portfolios from South Africa without the mandated 45% offshore limit inside ring-fenced mandates. Treasury and the Reserve Bank briefed investors on the proposal, which is open for comment until end-November and aims to attract management activity currently handled in offshore centres.

title: African Black-Owned Businesses Face $209bn Funding Gap, Report Finds
body: Black-owned and -led businesses across five African countries face an estimated $209 billion financing gap, according to a new report by British International Investment (BII) and Swedfund. The report examines the representation of black-owned and -led businesses, their financing needs and the barriers limiting their access to capital.

title: Wall Street to Host Africa Cocoa Finance, Investment Forum
body: The Africa Cocoa Finance & Investment Forum (ACFIF) 2026 will bring together investors, financial institutions, policymakers, cocoa industry leaders, development partners and entrepreneurs on October 26, 2026, at Wall Street in New York Financial District. The forum will link Africa cocoa sector with global capital, strategic partners and United States commercial opportunities.

title: Quickmart IPO reallocates shares as foreign institutions commit Sh7.2 billion
body: Kenyan grocer Quickmart revised allocations in its IPO after UK and US institutional investors, including MOBILIST, RWC Asset Management and the IFC, committed about Sh7.2 billion. Local and East African retail allocation was cut from 20% to 12%, with cornerstone investors reserved 48% of the 2 billion shares on offer at Sh7.50 each. The offer closes 30 October with Nairobi Securities Exchange listing expected 12 November.

title: Nigeria expands AfCFTA air cargo corridor as air freight costs fall below $2/kg
body: Nigeria launched an expanded Nigeria-East and Southern Africa Air Cargo Corridor in Lagos, partnering with RwandAir Cargo to connect Nigerian manufacturers to markets across East and Southern Africa. Industry, Trade and Investment Minister Jumoke Oduwole said the goal is to make cross-border trade easier and cheaper as air freight costs to Africa fall below $2 per kg, supporting non-oil export diversification.

title: Ruto urges African states to fund development through homegrown financial institutions
body: Kenyan President William Ruto told leaders at the 25th COMESA Heads of State summit in Harare that Africa must assume more responsibility for financing its own development by strengthening regional financial institutions. He urged governments to place a larger share of their foreign-exchange reserves with African banks and insurers, to channel development projects through them and to back their bonds and guarantees. Ruto highlighted that Africa holds more than $4 trillion in domestic financial assets, much of which remains in foreign accounts earning low returns while local projects await capital.

title: Dangote tasks African investors on funding home-grown businesses
body: Aliko Dangote, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, cautioned that African investors risk losing out on the prosperity generated by the continent’s industrial expansion if they continue channelling funds abroad instead of backing businesses at home. Speaking during a conversation with the Financial Times, Dangote outlined his ambition to expand the Group’s industrial investments across Africa. He argued that African capital should play a greater role in building globally competitive companies.

title: UK, Nigeria seal multi-sector deals as trade hits £8.1bn
body: The UK and Nigeria have sealed a raft of new multi-sector deals spanning agriculture, power, finance, and services, as bilateral trade hits £8.1 billion. Announced at the UK-Africa Investment Summit in London, the agreements signal deepened economic ties and unlock new opportunities for businesses in both nations. The deals cover areas such as technology, renewable energy, and financial services, aiming to create jobs and drive growth.

title: Dangote buys 25% stake in Kenya's oil pipeline network for $327 million
body: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote has acquired a 25% stake in Kenya Pipeline Company for about $327 million, expanding his energy business into East Africa's petroleum distribution infrastructure. The block was traded on the Nairobi Securities Exchange for 42.5 billion Kenyan shillings. Dangote announced the acquisition at the Financial Times Africa Summit in London, saying his company plans to invest $1.5 billion to expand the pipeline network. The investment supports his plans for a major refinery at Lamu, on Kenya's Indian Ocean coast.

title: ECOWAS energy ministers to consider battery storage, electricity market regulations
body: Energy ministers of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) are meeting in Accra to consider two regional instruments on battery energy storage and electricity market regulation. The first is a directive on Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to facilitate the integration of solar and other variable renewable energy sources into grids. The second is a proposed amendment to the ECOWAS Regional Electricity Market Levy to provide adequate resources for regional electricity institutions. The meeting forms part of ECOWAS efforts to strengthen regional energy integration and establish a functional electricity market.

title: UN and African Leaders Push for Greater Funding of Continental Data Systems
body: UN officials and African ministers urged stronger investment in data and statistical infrastructure across Africa to improve policy making and support the AfCFTA. Claver Gatete, UN Under-Secretary-General and head of the UN Economic Commission for Africa, said modernising core data platforms is essential for producing statistics that reflect Africa's development realities. Rwanda's finance minister, Yusuf Murangwa, described the continent's "data problem" as a structural weakness affecting both data availability and the capacity to analyse evidence for policy and investment decisions.

title: Dangote outlines $50 billion African investment programme at FT Africa Summit
body: Aliko Dangote, President and CEO of Dangote Industries, told the 2026 Financial Times Africa Summit in London that Africa's industrial ambitions hinge on long-term financing, reliable electricity and policies that convert raw resources into manufactured goods. He announced a $50 billion investment programme for 2026-2030 and said the continent's most urgent need today is power.

title: Ghana to ban unprocessed ore exports by 2030 and process half its cocoa locally
body: President John Mahama told the FT Africa Summit in London that Ghana will formally halt exports of unprocessed mineral ores by 2030 and process at least 50% of its cocoa beans domestically. He framed the move as building sovereign industrial capacity after noting Ghana lost about $154 million a year in official development assistance.

title: Afreenergy Solar secures EUR 12 million debt facility to expand Senegal C&I solar
body: UK-based Camco's Renewable Energy Performance Platform 2 provided a EUR 12 million senior debt facility to Afreenergy Solar to refinance its Senegalese rooftop solar portfolio and fund new solar PV and battery storage for commercial and industrial customers. Capacity is expected to grow from 2.7 MWp to 14.9 MWp of solar plus 5.7 MWh of storage.

title: South Africa's exports to China up 25% under Beijing's zero-tariff scheme
body: Chinese Ambassador Wu Peng told an event in Pretoria that South African exports to China rose nearly 25% year-on-year between May and August after Beijing's zero-tariff scheme for qualifying African goods took effect on 1 May. Trade Minister Parks Tau urged businesses to convert the preference, which runs to April 2028, into higher-value exports and local manufacturing.

title: Namibia offered Angola's Lobito refinery stake in possible southern Africa fuel shift
body: Angolan President João Lourenço invited Namibia to join the Lobito refinery's shareholders on October 19. The plant in Benguela province is planned to process 200,000 barrels of crude oil a day into diesel, petrol and other fuels. It still needs about $4.8 billion in financing to complete.

title: South Africa fires auditor Crowe over lead partner's US$24K fine
body: South Africa's Auditor-General (AGSA) ended Crowe's external audit contract after Business Day reported that a regulator had penalised Crowe's lead partner. The contract, due to run to January 2028, was terminated over concerns about silence regarding the sanction, raising audit-quality and reputational concerns.

title: Libya pipeline valve shut as Brent crude climbs to five-month high
body: Individuals shut the valve at the end of the 18-inch Hamada-Zawiya pipeline on October 22, according to the state National Oil Corporation. The line carries crude from the Hamada and Tahara fields to the Zawiya coast. The disruption came as Brent crude climbed above $114 a barrel on Friday, its highest level in over five months.

title: UBA secures Lagos court asset order in US$183,000 fuel dispute
body: A Lagos High Court granted United Bank for Africa (UBA) an asset order in a N242 million (about US$183,000) fuel dispute. TheCable reported the ruling on October 22. An asset order stops the defendant from moving money out of reach while the lawsuit runs.

Kenya annual inflation rose to 6.8% in September from 6.6% in August, per the Kenya National Bureau of Statistics. The Central Bank of Kenya expects pressures to persist through November, driven by food, fuel and energy prices and weather-constrained food supply.
title: Kenya inflation rises to 6.8% in September as food and energy costs climb

body: Somalia welcomed the first joint WTO and International Trade Center expert mission to Mogadishu, covering its decade-long accession and market-opening proposals in goods and services. A Working Party meeting expected in early 2027 would formally advance negotiations, with UK support via the ITC Making Trade Happen project.
title: Somalia hosts first WTO expert mission as accession bid advances

body: Buyers of Orca Energy Group's Tanzanian gas subsidiary have appealed the Fair Competition Commission's 5 October prohibition of the sale, filing with the Fair Competition Tribunal on 20 October. The outcome will shape whether foreign investors can acquire Tanzania's natural gas assets.
title: Orca Energy buyers appeal Tanzania ban on gas asset sale
Côte d'Ivoire breaks ground on 50MW Katiola solar plant
body: Energy Minister Mamadou Sangafowa-Coulibaly laid the first stone of the 50MW-peak Katiola solar plant at Lonankaha on 22 October. The project, developed by Katiola Solar Power with backing reported from Toyota and EDF, represents about 33 billion CFA francs (roughly US$56 million) with construction expected to take 15 months.

title: Dangote acquires about 25% of Kenya Pipeline Company as part of $50bn expansion plan
body: Aliko Dangote said he has acquired roughly a quarter of Kenya Pipeline Company, with reports citing a 24.76% stake for about $327 million, to expand his group's fuel storage and distribution across East Africa. He also told the Financial Times Africa Summit the group has earmarked $50 billion for investment through 2030, including a Djibouti-Addis Ababa supply route and a Southern African gateway in Namibia.

title: Ethiopia's FDI rises 49% to $1.43bn in first quarter of fiscal year
body: The Ethiopian Investment Commission reported foreign direct investment of $1.43bn for Q1 of fiscal 2026/27, up 49% year on year and 59% above its $900m target, crediting the market-based forex reforms introduced in July 2024 and expanded special economic zones. The projects are projected to create more than 22,000 jobs and $238m in export revenue.

title: South Africa's exports to China jump about 25% under Beijing's zero-tariff scheme
body: Chinese Ambassador Wu Peng said South African exports to China rose nearly 25% year on year between May and August after Beijing's duty-free scheme for qualifying African goods took effect on 1 May, with imports from China up 23% over the same period. Trade Minister Parks Tau urged businesses to convert the temporary preference, which runs to April 2028, into higher-value exports and local manufacturing.

title: Ghana to ban unprocessed mineral ore exports by 2030 and process half its cocoa locally
body: President John Mahama told the Financial Times Africa Summit in London that Ghana will halt exports of unprocessed mineral ores, including bauxite, manganese, iron and lithium, by 2030 and process at least 50% of its cocoa beans domestically. He framed the move as building sovereign industrial capacity after the country lost about $154m a year in official development assistance.

title: Afreximbank and AfCFTA Secretariat sign auto-industry MoU at Africa Automotive Investment Forum
body: At the Africa Automotive Investment Forum in El Alamein, the AfCFTA Secretariat and the African Association of Automotive Manufacturers signed an MoU covering automotive rules of origin, customs procedures, supplier development and mineral beneficiation, supporting the AfCFTA Automotive Investment Plan. A joint venture between South Africa's Malben Engineering and Egypt's El Araby Group to manufacture components was also announced.

title: Egypt's TMG signs four state projects with targeted investment of about $202 billion
body: Hisham Talaat Moustafa's Talaat Moustafa Group agreed four projects with the Egyptian state across Abu Qir, North Madinaty, central Alexandria and the North Coast, with targeted investment of EGP 11 trillion (about $202 billion). Analysts note the figure is targeted investment, not revenue, and detailed terms have not been published.

title: Egypt fintech MNT-Halan debuts above offer price at about $775 million valuation
body: MNT-Halan, the Egyptian fintech founded by Mounir Nakhla, closed its first trading day 6.6% above its offer price, valuing the company at about $775 million. The listing adds to a run of African consumer-fintech flotations this year.

title: Nigerian startups raise $635m in nine months, leading Africa
body: Nigerian startups raised $635 million between January and September 2026, topping Africa by country and running 2.6x the $247 million raised in the same stretch of 2025, per the Africa: The Big Deal tracker. Four companies - Moove, Flutterwave, Jumia and Yellow Card - account for roughly $440 million of the total, while 77 Nigerian ventures raised at least $100,000, up from 70 a year earlier. It is Nigerias best January-September result since 2022.
source: Tech Insider (citing Africa: The Big Deal)

title: African ports warned over cyberattack risk to trade
body: Speaking at the African Ports Conference in Casablanca, Nigerian Ports Authority MD Abubakar Dantsoho, who also leads the Port Management Association of West and Central Africa, warned that rising cyberattacks could disrupt African ports and international trade, citing incidents at South Africas Transnet, Japans Port of Nagoya and DP World terminals. He called for regional cyber threat intelligence sharing, common data standards and for African ports to integrate cybersecurity into their broader security frameworks as they adopt AI and interconnected systems.

title: AfDB approves $487 million reform and climate resilience package for Morocco
body: The African Development Bank's Board approved $487 million for Morocco's third economic governance and climate resilience programme. It supports public enterprise restructuring, a modernised PPP framework and private-sector investment mobilisation, alongside water and electricity sector governance reform to strengthen climate resilience.

title: AfDB approves $487 million package for Morocco's economic governance and climate resilience
body: The African Development Bank's Board approved a $487 million financing package for Morocco on 22 October, supporting Phase III of the Economic Governance and Climate Change Resilience Support Program. The funds back water efficiency, seawater desalination and inter-basin transfer projects alongside renewable energy deployment and green hydrogen development.

title: Burundi signs $1.4 billion, 25-year deal with Weza Power to expand electricity access
body: Burundi has signed a $1.4 billion, 25-year public-private partnership with Weza Power to expand and operate its electricity distribution network. The deal targets new or improved electricity access for approximately 8 million people by 2030 in one of Africa's least electrified countries.

title: Ghana set to overtake Ethiopia as Africa's eighth-largest economy
body: The IMF's October 2026 World Economic Outlook projects Ghana's GDP at $128.64 billion (approx. GH₵1.50 trillion) for 2026, overtaking Ethiopia as Africa's eighth-largest economy. The Fund is also forecasting a 5.7% growth rate for Ghana in 2026. Ghana's economic composition is diversified relative to its West African peers, with gold and cocoa exports remaining significant while the oil and gas sector increasingly contributes to GDP and fiscal revenue.

title: AfDB and Equity Bank Kenya sign US$60m trade finance guarantee
body: The African Development Bank and Equity Bank Kenya signed a US$60 million Trade Finance Transaction Guarantee Facility covering eligible letters of credit and comparable trade instruments issued by Equity Bank Kenya. The facility can guarantee up to 100% of a confirming bank's non-payment risk, aiming to unlock more trade finance for Kenyan SMEs and local corporates and to deepen intra-African trade under the AfCFTA framework.

title: Dangote acquires 25% of Kenya Pipeline for $327m and expands East and Southern Africa footprint
body: Aliko Dangote disclosed at the Financial Times Africa Summit in London that his group has acquired a 25% stake in Kenya Pipeline Company for approximately $327.4 million, buying about 4.5 billion shares. He also revealed plans for new fuel-storage projects in Djibouti, Ethiopia, Cameroon and Namibia — including a 330-million-litre tank farm at Walvis Bay, Namibia — as his group builds an integrated African refining, storage and distribution network.

title: UNCTAD: Africa attracted about $70 billion in FDI in 2025
body: The World Investment Report 2026 shows Africa attracted about $70 billion in foreign direct investment in 2025, below the $94 billion recorded in 2024 but still the third-highest level since 1990 and roughly a third above the continent's long-term average. Egypt remained Africa's largest FDI recipient at about $15 billion, and African least developed countries took in about $33 billion. UNCTAD warns the harder task is converting strategic-sector interest into lasting industrial capacity, jobs and technology transfer.

title: African Energy Week 2026 closes with $17bn in commitments; African Energy Bank to start operations in November
body: African Energy Week 2026 concluded in Cape Town with more than $17 billion in total commitments, including a Deal Room of 15 oil, gas and power projects seeking over $16 billion. APPO Secretary-General Farid Ghezali said the Abuja-based African Energy Bank, promoted with Afreximbank, is expected to commence operations in November 2026 with $500 million in initial capital and longer-term ambitions of up to $10 billion. Ghana also reported a roughly 30 percent rise in crude production, and Eni confirmed Coral North FLNG drilling in Mozambique begins in November.

title: Kenya begins extension of Mombasa-Nairobi railway to Kisumu
body: Kenya Railways said construction of the Mombasa-Nairobi standard gauge railway extension to Kisumu has begun, with the first phase due within two years. Reaching Kisumu will connect the line to Lake Victoria and open regional markets in Uganda, DR Congo, South Sudan and Rwanda to the Port of Mombasa. The announcement came at the Financial Street Forum's Nairobi session, where China and African states pledged deeper Belt and Road cooperation in infrastructure, trade and financing, aligned with the AU's Agenda 2063.

title: AXIAN secures $62m from FMO for Ivory Coast solar plant
body: AXIAN Group has signed up to EUR 55.5 million in 20-year loans from Dutch development bank FMO for Kong Solaire, a 50 MWp solar plant in northern Ivory Coast co-developed with Africa Via and InfraCo. Construction is under way with operations expected in 2028, supplying about 96 GWh a year to state utility CI-Energies under a 25-year purchase agreement — enough for roughly 240,000 people.

title: Africa needs 700 data centres by 2035 to power digital trade under AfCFTA
body: AfCFTA secretary-general Wamkele Mene said at the AfCFTA Digital Trade Forum in Lagos that the continent needs about 700 data centres by 2035 to support cross-border electronic trade, calling for stepped-up investment in energy and digital infrastructure. The Africa Data Centre Association noted most carrier-neutral facilities and hyperscale campuses remain foreign-owned and private-equity financed.

title: AfCFTA Implementation Driving Major Welfare Gains in East Africa
body: A new report by the UN Economic Commission for Africa (ECA) projects that AfCFTA implementation in East Africa could yield welfare gains of USD 1.8 billion, boosting intra-African exports by over USD 1.1 billion and creating over 2 million new jobs.

title: South Africa sets a timetable for non-bank payment access
body: The South African Reserve Bank said rules governing payment activities and exemptions will be published by November, with initial non-bank participation expected around March 2027 ahead of a broader mid-2027 launch. The framework will allow telecommunications companies, fintechs and retailers to connect directly to national payments infrastructure, covering e-money issuance, merchant acquiring and payment initiation.

title: UK businesses secure £330 million of African infrastructure contracts
body: British businesses are set to secure more than £330 million of export contracts to help deliver nine major infrastructure projects across Guinea and Benin. The contracts span education, clean water, electricity transmission and government infrastructure, supported by £1.1 billion in financing and guarantees from UK Export Finance. The deals were announced as the fifth UK-West and Central Francophone Africa Trade and Investment Forum opened in Conakry.

title: Nigeria targets 250,000bpd from 22 oil block awardees
body: The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission is targeting about 250,000 barrels per day of crude oil production from 22 petroleum prospecting licence awardees within the next five years. Commission chief executive Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan disclosed this at an on-boarding workshop in Lagos themed 'From Award to Production: Delivering Nigeria's Upstream Petroleum Potential Under the Petroleum Industry Act, 2021'.

title: AfDB settles EUR 1 billion Social Benchmark bond to fund social projects
body: The African Development Bank settled a EUR 1 billion, 5-year Social Benchmark bond due October 2031, with proceeds to finance eligible social projects across Africa under its Sustainable Bond Framework. Priced on October 14, the bond pays a 3.500% annual coupon and was managed by Barclays, Deutsche Bank, HSBC and Natixis.

title: IMF: sub-Saharan Africa set to outgrow China in 2026
body: At its annual meetings the IMF projected sub-Saharan Africa to grow 4.5% in 2026, 0.1 percentage point above China’s forecast — the first time in decades the region outpaces China. Ethiopia, Guinea, Rwanda and Cote d’Ivoire are projected to grow at or above 6%.
source: Business Tech Africa (citing IMF annual meetings)

title: MNT-Halan raises ~$150m in Egyptian Exchange debut
body: Egypt’s largest fintech by loan book listed on the EGX, selling 320 million shares (20% of the Egyptian operating company) at EGP 24.50 for roughly EGP 7.84 billion (~$150m). The private tranche was 11.2x and retail 43.6x oversubscribed; it is the largest Egyptian IPO in dollar terms since 2021.

title: African corporate bond issuance hits $13.3bn, strongest in five years
body: African companies raised $13.3 billion in hard-currency bonds in the first nine months of 2026, including $3.25 billion in private placements — the fastest pace in five years and second only to 2021’s $17 billion, per Bank of America. Eleven countries are represented this year, up from eight in 2021, with no defaults since 2020.
source: Business Tech Africa (citing Bank of America)

title: Second machinery shipment arrives for Dangote’s planned Kenyan refinery
body: The Port of Lamu received a second consignment — 154 pieces of heavy equipment aboard MV Great Glory — for the planned $17bn Dangote East African refinery designed to process up to 700,000 barrels per day. The project follows groundbreaking in Lamu County on 30 September attended by President Ruto and Aliko Dangote.

title: Kenya overtakes Ethiopia as East Africa's largest economy
body: IMF October 2026 World Economic Outlook data puts Kenya's GDP at $151.15bn, edging past Ethiopia's $127.15bn after the birr lost more than a third of its value following the end of exchange-rate controls tied to a $3.4bn IMF programme. In real terms Ethiopia actually grew faster in 2025 (9.2% vs Kenya's 4.6%) - the reversal is currency-driven. Kenya now ranks seventh among Africa's largest economies.

title: Ethiopia's PM pushes stronger Kenya-Ethiopia energy and trade ties at Mashujaa Day
body: Speaking at Kenya's Mashujaa Day celebrations, Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed called for deeper Kenya-Ethiopia cooperation on energy and trade, building on the Lamu corridor and cross-border power links. The appeal came alongside regional momentum on the Dangote East Africa refinery at Lamu and expanding East African connectivity projects.

title: Ramaphosa warns South Africa to prepare for possible loss of AGOA access
body: President Cyril Ramaphosa said South Africa should prepare for the possibility of being removed from the US African Growth and Opportunity Act, even though Congress has renewed the scheme to the end of 2028. He noted the renewal now awaits President Trump's signature, with South Africa the programme's largest beneficiary amid strained US-South Africa ties.

title: Africa Commerce and Industry Summit opens in Nairobi targeting $64.71bn in trade deals
body: More than 5,000 delegates from 50 countries gathered in Nairobi for the Africa Commerce and Industry Summit 2026, convened by the Kenya National Chamber of Commerce and Industry to advance AfCFTA-driven trade and investment. Organisers highlighted cumulative China-Africa trade agreements worth $64.71bn across four expo editions, and Kenya and South Africa chambers announced a partnership of intent for a private-sector joint business council.

Egypt's largest fintech by loan book began trading on the Egyptian Exchange after selling 320 million existing shares (20% of its Egyptian operating company) at EGP 24.50, raising about EGP 7.84 billion (~$150 million). The retail tranche was 43.6 times oversubscribed with total demand of about EGP 126 billion, and the listing values the Egyptian business at roughly $745 million. It is the largest Egyptian IPO in dollar terms since 2021 and the biggest by a private company in a decade.
title: MNT-Halan raises ~$150m in landmark Egyptian Exchange debut

body: African companies raised $13.3 billion in hard-currency bonds in the first nine months of 2026, the strongest pace in five years according to Bank of America, including $3.25 billion in private placements. Eleven African countries are represented this year, up from eight in 2021, with issuers including First Quantum Minerals, Azule Energy and Sasol. Rating upgrades have outnumbered downgrades and the segment has recorded no defaults since 2020.
source: Business Tech Africa (citing Bank of America)
title: African corporate bonds raise $13.3bn in 2026, strongest pace in five years

body: Botswana's energy regulator said a bill allowing electricity trading and independent transmission providers will go to Parliament in November. The changes would let producers sell power to buyers other than the state utility, part of a push to open the market to private investors and position Botswana as a regional energy hub. The country currently imports about 35% of its electricity.
title: Botswana to table power trading and private transmission bill in November

body: Senegal's dollar bonds had their steepest fall since early September after National Assembly head Ousmane Sonko threatened to block the revised 2026 budget, and the plenary vote planned for October 23 was pushed to next week. Former prime minister Amadou Ba warned that FCFA 540 billion (about $924 million) of energy subsidies would lack funding without the revised budget.
source: Rio Times Online (citing Dakaractu, Seneweb, Le Soleil)
title: Senegal bonds fall as budget standoff delays revised 2026 budget vote
ECOWAS Business Council unveils 'Power W.A.' private-sector power initiative
body: The ECOWAS Business Council, chaired by Aliko Dangote, unveiled a private-sector-led initiative tagged 'Power W.A.' to prioritize regional energy sufficiency as a catalyst for West African industrialisation. It will establish industrial power corridors backed by a regional electricity demand-and-supply gap study, with funding to be mobilised from Afreximbank, the Africa Finance Corporation and the IFC, while ECOWAS and national governments provide policy guarantees.

title: Ghana shipped non-traditional exports to 47 African countries under AfCFTA in 2025
body: Ghana's National AfCFTA Coordination Office says the country exported non-traditional goods to 47 African countries in 2025 under the continental free trade agreement, and was the first to set up a dedicated national AfCFTA coordination office. Coordinator Dode Seidu called for stronger SME education so smaller businesses can access the wider African market.

title: Nigeria: next growth phase to be financed by private capital, petrol subsidy stays gone
body: Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele said at Chatham House in London that Nigeria's next phase of growth will be financed by private capital, domestic and foreign, rather than state borrowing, and ruled out any return to petrol subsidies. He said inflation has fallen to 14.63% from 21% a year ago and needs to reach low single digits, dismissed the IMF's 4.2% 2026 growth forecast as too conservative, and said the government is targeting average annual growth of about 7% over the next five years.

title: South Africa narrows budget deficit to 3.9% of GDP but cuts growth forecast to 1.2%
body: In the 2026 mid-term budget policy statement, Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana said the consolidated deficit narrows to 3.9% of GDP this year, debt stabilises at 78.4% of GDP in 2025/26 — the first such pause in nearly two decades — and gross tax revenue was revised up by R17.1 billion. Treasury cut its 2026 growth forecast to 1.2% from 1.6%, and announced fuel-levy relief of R3 per litre on diesel and R1.50 on petrol from 4 November, costing R10 billion in foregone revenue.

title: South Africa budget: deficit narrows to 3.9% as debt finally stabilises
body: Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana tabled the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement, showing the consolidated deficit narrowing to 3.9% of GDP in 2026/27 and debt stabilising at 78.4% of GDP - the first pause in nearly two decades - with gross tax revenue revised up by R17.1 billion. Growth forecasts were cut to 1.2% for 2026 from 1.6%, rising to 2% by 2029, and a temporary fuel levy cut takes effect on 4 November.

title: Nigeria: growth will be financed by private capital, says Finance Minister Oyedele
body: Speaking at Chatham House in London, Finance Minister Wale Oyedele said Nigeria will turn to private investors at home and abroad rather than state borrowing for its next growth phase, ruling out any return to petrol subsidies. He said inflation has fallen to 14.63% from 21% a year ago and must reach low single digits, and called IMF growth forecasts of 4.2% for 2026 too conservative, targeting about 7% average annual growth over five years.

title: Dangote buys 25% stake in Kenya Pipeline to secure supply chain
body: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote announced that his company bought a 25% stake in Kenya Pipeline Company, a move designed to secure product distribution for the 700,000-bpd refinery he plans to build at Kenya's Lamu port. Kenya sold 65% of KPC via an IPO earlier this year as it sought to raise revenue amid limited fiscal space.

title: South African bonds rally on new bond buyback programme
body: South Africa's benchmark 2035 government bond rallied strongly, with its yield falling 14.5 basis points to 8.59%, after the National Treasury announced plans to reduce the amount of fixed-rate bonds sold weekly and launch a bond buyback programme as part of efforts to show fiscal discipline and bring down debt levels.

title: Nigeria says next growth phase will be financed by private capital
body: Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele told Chatham House in London that Nigeria will increasingly rely on private investors at home and abroad rather than state borrowing to finance its next phase of growth, and ruled out any return to petrol subsidies.

title: Nedbank offer for Kenyatta-family-linked NCBA declared unconditional; 66% stake secured
body: South Africa Nedbank Group completed its acquisition of a controlling stake in Kenya NCBA Group, with the offer declared unconditional on October 21 after securing about 66% of issued shares (1,087,362,891 shares). Trading in NCBA on the Nairobi Securities Exchange was suspended from October 21 ahead of a block trade and settlement on November 3, marking one of the largest cross-border banking deals in East Africa.

title: IMF: Africa's 30% share of critical minerals positions it for AI and clean-energy demand
body: IMF African Department director Zeine Zeidane said Africa's 30 percent share of global critical-mineral reserves positions the continent to benefit from surging demand for AI infrastructure and clean energy technologies. The Fund's October Regional Economic Outlook Update estimates that adopting and scaling AI across Africa could lift growth by more than four percentage points over ten years, and that closing half the continent's governance and business-environment gaps could raise GDP by more than 20 percent over a decade. He cautioned mineral wealth alone will not guarantee prosperity without reforms to mobilise domestic savings and improve the investment climate.

title: South Africa tables mid-term budget with a proposed fiscal anchor amid oil shock and weak growth
body: Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana tabled the 2026 Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement in Cape Town, expected to introduce a 'fiscal anchor' to bind future governments to spending rules. He faces a harder environment than February: the IMF expects oil around $96 a barrel in 2026 (~41% above 2025), the economy contracted 0.2% in Q2 ending six quarters of growth, and the Reserve Bank has hiked twice. Tax collections ran ahead of plan, with economists seeing the main deficit narrowing toward 3.3-3.6% of GDP.

title: UK Export Finance backs nine infrastructure projects in Guinea and Benin
body: UK Export Finance said nine infrastructure projects in Guinea and Benin are linked to more than £330m in prospective export contracts for British firms, supported by £1.1bn in financing and guarantees. Named deals include school and water projects and a Conakry power transmission line in Guinea, and a government administrative complex in Benin. The agency also raised its exposure capacity for future West and Central African projects by £1.7bn.
